planName: Harness Gate Integrity and Cross-Harness Parity
summary: Act on the 2026-08-28 harness research packet (docs/research/research01-20260828-agentic-harness-review.html). The harness runs green everywhere; the defects are in what the gates guarantee. Decisions taken with the human: build-guard becomes a hard boundary (fail closed, bypass set covered); tdd-guard binds the green command to the sealed red command by argv digest; the four dangling skill references (read-the-damn-docs, find-docs, grill-with-docs, full-output-enforcement) are dropped rather than authored; the unused controlplane contract surface is kept and covered by tests. Wave 1 carries eight independent tracks with disjoint ownership; wave 2 lands the follow-ons that touch the same files (guard blind spots, CI wiring, documentation) once wave 1 behaviour is final.

components.name: tdd-guard (guard/, cmd/tdd-guard)
components.purpose: Mechanical red->green gate; after this plan it proves the sealed red argv went green, not merely that some command passed.

components.name: build-guard / build-hooks (scripts/hooks)
components.purpose: PreToolUse boundary for main-branch pushes and tmpfs cargo targets; after this plan it fails closed and its probe corpus is a test fixture.

components.name: Installers (scripts/*.sh)
components.purpose: Symlink-only projection of this repo into each harness with ownership checks on install and uninstall; portable to stock macOS.

components.name: Agent definitions (agents/)
components.purpose: Harness-specific frontmatter over shared procedure; skill references must resolve and gate wiring must be declared per harness.

components.name: Skill scripts (skills/*/scripts)
components.purpose: Deterministic planner, build-wave, review, research and loop helpers; idempotent GitHub reconciliation and safe overlap detection.

components.name: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
components.purpose: Discovers every skill test suite, pins Python, and runs the lint gates the hooks assume.

components.name: Docs (README, CHANGELOG, docs/adr)
components.purpose: Describe the enforced behaviour accurately after the code changes land.

issues.title: tdd-guard: bind verify's green command to the sealed red command
issues.body: Research F1-02, F1-13, F1-17. Today `tdd-guard seal --red-command false` followed by `tdd-guard verify --green-command true` passes: seal only requires the red argv to exit non-zero and verify only requires the green argv to exit 0 after the seal (guard/actions.go:42, :98-103). Scope: record the red ArgvDigest in the seal; make verify refuse a green argv whose digest differs from the sealed red argv (exit non-zero with a message naming both digests); re-compute sealed-test digests after the green command runs and fail verify if any sealed test changed during the run (closes the TOCTOU at actions.go:87-103); surface the bound argv in `status`. Keep the seal file schema backward-compatible or migrate explicitly with a test. Update guard/*_test.go and the builder agent text that describes the seal/verify contract only where it states the argv rule.

acceptanceTests.oracle: After a seal with red argv X, verify with green argv Y != X exits non-zero and the seal remains unverified

acceptanceTests.name: verify-accepts-same-argv
acceptanceTests.oracle: After a seal with red argv X (exit 1), verify with argv X (exit 0) succeeds and status reports green with the bound digest

acceptanceTests.name: verify-detects-sealed-test-edit-during-green
acceptanceTests.oracle: A green command that rewrites a sealed test file then restores it causes verify to exit non-zero

acceptanceTests.name: false-then-true-no-longer-passes
acceptanceTests.oracle: Scratch repo: seal --red-command false then verify --green-command true exits non-zero

issues.title: build-guard: fail closed and cover the bypass and false-positive corpus
issues.body: Research F2-05, F2-06, F2-07, F2-08, F2-19, F2-20, F2-03. Decision: build-guard is a hard boundary. Scope in scripts/hooks/build-guard and build-hooks: (1) exit 2 with a reason when jq is missing, the payload is unparseable, or the harness payload shape yields no command; build-hooks exits 2 when tdd-guard is absent instead of 127. (2) Deny: bare `git push` and `git push <remote>` with no refspec, `git push <remote> HEAD`, `git push <remote> master`, `git branch -f main`, `git branch -f master`, `git update-ref refs/heads/main`, `gh pr merge`, `git checkout main`/`git switch main` followed by `git merge` on the same line, `jj bookmark set main` combined with `jj git push`, and cargo `--target-dir` / `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` / `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR` pointing at /tmp, /dev/shm or $TMPDIR with or without quotes and with or without a trailing slash. (3) Stop denying `main-*`/`main.*` branch names, commit-message text (`-m "... main ..."`), `git merge-base`, and quoted strings passed to echo/grep. Use a small tokenizer (strip quoted args before matching) rather than more regex. (4) Move the probe list into scripts/hooks/tests/guard-corpus.txt (expected|command per line) and have test_hooks.sh assert every line; make test_hooks.sh hermetic by running project-bootstrap under a temporary HOME/BIN so it never writes to the real ~/.local/bin. Keep POSIX ERE only; no \b, no -P.

acceptanceTests.oracle: Every line of scripts/hooks/tests/guard-corpus.txt (>= 40 entries covering the research bypass and false-positive sets) produces the expected allow/deny decision for the Claude and agy payload shapes

issues.title: Installers: symlink-only, ownership-checked, fail-fast, and portable to stock macOS
issues.body: Research F2-04, F2-11, F2-13, F2-14, F2-15, F2-16, F2-17, F5-08. Scope across scripts/install-harness.sh, scripts/project-bootstrap.sh, scripts/bootstrap-tools.sh: (1) project-bootstrap.sh --install symlinks the hook scripts with ln -sfn exactly like bootstrap-tools.sh; no `install -m755` copies remain. (2) A shared helper `link_owned SRC DST` that creates the link only if DST is absent or is a symlink resolving into $ROOT, and otherwise prints a clear refusal and returns non-zero; `unlink_owned DST` removes only such symlinks. Use both for every agent, skill, hook and codex TOML link. (3) --uninstall also removes ~/.local/bin/build-* and ~/.local/bin/tdd-guard links it owns and reports what it left behind. (4) Replace `mapfile` + `find -printf` with a portable `for d in "$ROOT"/skills/*/` loop; scripts run under bash 3.2 syntax. (5) `set -euo pipefail` with explicit error messages so 'done.' only prints on success; validate agents/codex/*.md frontmatter before touching any harness. (6) project-bootstrap.sh writes the local exclude via `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` so worktrees and jj workspaces are covered. (7) Never hide a sudo prompt: run installer commands without redirecting stdin/stderr or skip them with a message when not a tty.

acceptanceTests.oracle: With HOME set to a temp dir containing a real directory at .claude/skills/jj and a user file at .claude/agents/builder.md, install-harness.sh --install exits non-zero, names both targets, and leaves them byte-identical

issues.title: Agents: drop dangling skill references and declare gate wiring per harness
issues.body: Research F4-01, F4-02, F4-03, F4-04, F4-05, F4-06, F4-07, F4-08, F4-22, F2-10, F2-09. Decision: drop the four dangling references. Scope across agents/** and skills/docs/**: (1) Remove read-the-damn-docs and find-docs from all research agents, grill-with-docs from all docs agents, and full-output-enforcement from all builders; where a Skills section becomes empty, delete the section. (2) Add a mechanical check to skills/docs/scripts/docs_check.py (and its tests) that every skill named in a `## Skills` section or a `skills:` frontmatter across agents/**/*.md exists as a directory under skills/. (3) Antigravity builder hooks.json gains a Stop-equivalent hook calling `build-hooks agy Stop` if the harness supports one; if it does not, the agy builder agent.md states that the Stop-time verify gate is manual and the builder must run `tdd-guard verify` itself before handing off. (4) Codex builder: document in its frontmatter comment and body that no PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks exist on Codex and that build-guard and tdd-guard are invoked explicitly by the builder (`tdd-guard hook` is not available; call seal/verify directly). (5) Codex and agy builders declare the mechanism they use to hand the change-set to a code-reviewer, or the step is reworded to 'run the code-review skill' if spawning is not available. (6) Align model tiers: agy builder no longer runs on `flash`; use the harness's strongest tier for builder and a mid tier for code-reviewer/docs, matching Codex's high/medium/medium/low ladder; set mainAgent only on builder and docs. (7) agy builder prose reflects its automatic format/lint hooks. (8) docs_check.py INSTRUCTION_FILES includes GEMINI.md.

issues.title: build skill: fix recursive-glob overlap false negative and bound builder re-dispatch
issues.body: Research F3-07, F3-08, F3-20, F4-18. Scope in skills/build/**: (1) globs_overlap in scripts/waves.py must report overlap for `src/**` vs `src/a/b/c.py` in both argument orders; implement with PurePath.full_match on 3.13+ and an fnmatch-based fallback, and treat a plain path as its own literal glob. (2) Exclude wave 0 (ungrouped) from the hard-fail overlap check; warn only. (3) Emit the warning or raise, not both. (4) Document the `status:done` label in SKILL.md. (5) Add a re-dispatch cap to SKILL.md: a builder that returns `blocked` may be re-dispatched at most twice per issue, after which the issue is marked stalled in the wave summary and the loop escalates to the human.

issues.title: planner/code-review: id normalisation, single-pass token substitution, safer reconciliation
issues.body: Research F3-03, F3-04, F3-06, F3-09, F3-10, F3-12. Scope in skills/planner/** and skills/code-review/**: (1) validate_plan stores the stripped planId and issue keys (or rejects padded values) so markers round-trip and a second reconcile of an unchanged plan is a no-op. (2) Both render_plan.py and render_review.py substitute template tokens in a single re.sub pass so user text containing a token name is left verbatim; the research renderer already does this. (3) mermaid_label neutralises `#`, `;`, backticks and angle brackets. (4) Planner reconcile skips reopening issues that are closed and carry the status:done label or were closed by a merged PR (state_reason completed) unless --reopen-done is passed; milestone adoption by title preserves an existing description by appending the marker. (5) reconcile_findings only closes an issue when its recorded severity (from the marker or a label) is at or above the current --min-severity, so a stricter threshold never closes live defects. Update SKILL.md text for both skills accordingly.

issues.title: research: make conflict detection mean disagreement, not distinct wording
issues.body: Research recommendation R-16. merge_research.py flags a conflict whenever a topic has more than one distinct free-text position, so the 2026-08-28 packet reported 20 conflicts of which two were real. Scope in skills/research/**: (1) A finding may carry an optional `contradicts` boolean or the agent envelope gains a `stance` field constrained to {supports, contradicts, neutral} per topic; a conflict is reported only when a topic carries both supports and contradicts (or at least one contradicts). Choose the stance form, keep the existing example fixtures valid (defaulting to neutral), and update the research agent envelope text in all three harness variants only if the field is mandatory — prefer optional. (2) merge_research.nonempty_string strips like the other scripts. (3) Land the new render_research.py, templates and tests already in the working tree, and add the planner/code-review byte-identity requirement for report.css to the research SKILL.md (already drafted).

acceptanceTests.oracle: Two findings on one topic where one carries the contradicting stance produce exactly one conflict listing both positions

issues.title: guard: digest full untracked files, lock the touch log, cover the controlplane contract
issues.body: Research F1-03, F1-09, F1-10, F1-11, F1-12, F1-14, F1-18, F5-12. Decision: keep the controlplane surface. Scope in guard/** and controlplane/** after G1 lands: (1) digestFileStreaming hashes the whole stream (still bounded memory) and includes the byte length, so edits past 10 MiB invalidate diff-review; drop the truncation assertion from hardening_test.go. (2) recordTouchedRepositories takes an advisory file lock (or O_EXCL temp + rename retry) so concurrent hooks cannot drop entries; add a two-process test. (3) workingDiff skips non-regular untracked entries. (4) Delete filesMatchingGlob. (5) ValidIdentifier rejects `..` segments and leading `/` or the doc comment is corrected — pick reject. (6) Add tests for DecodeWorkflowResult, DecodeRoute, DecodeSelection, SealGoal/ValidateGoal, SealAssignment/ValidateAssignment, SealDispatch/ValidateDispatch and CanonicalDigest covering the fail-closed paths; controlplane coverage >= 85%. (7) Usage text derives from os.Args[0] and --help/-h exit 0. (8) unsealedSourceChanges un-escapes C-quoted porcelain paths.

issues.title: CI: discover every skill suite, pin Python, add ruff and shellcheck gates
issues.body: Research F5-06, F5-07, F3-02, F3-14, F4-12. Scope in .github/** and skills/docs/tests/**: (1) ci.yml loops over skills/*/tests (`for d in skills/*/tests; do python3 -m unittest discover -s "$d" -p 'test_*.py'; done`) so review-fix-loop and any future suite run. (2) actions/setup-python pins 3.13. (3) Add `ruff check skills/` and `shellcheck -S warning scripts/*.sh scripts/hooks/build-*` steps; fix the 44 ruff findings and the one SC2088 so the gates pass. (4) Add scripts/tests/test_install.sh (from I1) and `go test -count=1 -race ./...` to the pipeline. (5) The docs test that guards ci.yml asserts the loop form rather than a fixed skill list.

risks.title: Argv binding breaks existing seal files or the build skill's seal/verify invocation
risks.mitigation: Version the seal schema, accept legacy seals with an explicit warning for one release, and run the build skill's documented seal/verify sequence in an e2e test before merging.

risks.title: A hard-boundary build-guard blocks legitimate builder commands in the field
risks.mitigation: The corpus fixture includes the false-positive set from research; any new deny rule must ship with allow cases; failures print the matched rule so a human can extend the corpus.

risks.title: Ownership-checked install refuses on machines with hand-made links and stalls adoption
risks.mitigation: Refusal message names the exact path and the `--force` flag that replaces a symlink (never a real file or directory); bootstrap report lists foreign targets before install.

risks.title: Antigravity has no Stop hook, so the agy TDD gate stays manual
risks.mitigation: Verify the Antigravity hook contract first; if absent, make the manual `tdd-guard verify` instruction explicit and assert it by test so the gap is documented rather than silent.

risks.title: Wave-2 docs describe behaviour that a wave-1 track changed again during review
risks.mitigation: D1 starts only after all wave-1 PRs merge; its tests grep the code for the claims (usage text, corpus file, loop form) rather than restating them.

risks.title: Hashing full untracked files removes the 10 MiB bound on time for huge generated artifacts
risks.mitigation: Keep a hard ceiling (e.g. 256 MiB) above which the file is recorded as 'oversize' with its size and mtime instead of a content digest, and test both branches.
